Jules and Connor to schedule infra deep-dive (Redwood Private reference arch) next week
MarketForge marketing to confirm joint solution one-pager and co-branding assets by 2025-11-20
action_items: Samir - send marketplace listing template and example screenshots - due 2025-11-13
Jules - prepare reference architecture diagram (Redwood Private + MarketForge connector) - due 2025-11-17

summary: Partner engineering sync to align on listing requirements for MarketForge marketplace, reference architecture for a joint on-prem/private deployment pattern, and next steps for a pilot. Discussed onboarding flows, security/compliance requirements (SOC2, KMS, SSO), API contract, and go-to-market assets.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-06 15:00 PST | Duration: ~46m | Attendees: Samir(Patel) Redwood AE, Jules Ortega Redwood SE, Maya Lin MF Head Partnerships, Connor Reyes MF Platform Eng, Priya Singh MF Solutions Arch

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll run about 45 minutes. quick agenda: marketplace listing reqs, reference arch for private / vpc integration, and next steps for a small pilot. sound good?
[00:18] Maya: yep that works, excited to get this moving. we have some questions about what the marketplace listing needs to include and how the private deployment would actually show up on our side.
[00:28] Jules: cool, i'll start with the listing pieces — typically we need a short description, tech spec, icon/screenshots, pricing model, plus a short integration guide. i'll share our template after.
[00:41] Connor: are there any runtime artifacts we need to expose? like metrics endpoints, health checks, or should we just link to redwood console?
[00:50] Jules: good question. for hosted listings it's mostly links to docs and a short matrix of supported features. for dedicated/private listings we ask for a reference arch diagram and an ops checklist (network rules, k8s, if on-prem etc). you can link to redwood console for runtime metrics — but for private we often ship a lightweight exporter that plugs into your monitoring.
[01:12] Priya: when you say private, do you mean the full private control plane or just VPC peering? need to understand data paths.
[01:20] Samir: yeah there are a couple of patterns. Redwood Dedicated is reserved capacity in our infra; Redwood Private is VPC or on-prem with a customer-managed control plane. for the marketplace joint solution we usually show both options: quick self-serve hosted path and a reference arch for private deployment.
[01:38] Maya: okay, our customers will care about data residency and audit logs. what level of SOC/ISO info do you provide on the listing?
[01:46] Jules: we can include SOC2/ISO attestations and a short security FAQ. we also provide integration notes for KMS/HSM and SSO/SAML. expect to include a link to our security pack (we'll share the PDF).
[02:05] Connor: on KMS — do you support customer managed keys for private deployments? and is there a specific KMS provider you prefer?
[02:12] Jules: yes we support CMKs via standard KMS integrations; customers use AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM depending on deployment. for on-prem there's a KMS connector pattern in the ref arch.
[02:24] Priya: excellent. can you describe the reference arch at a high level? we're thinking about where the MarketForge connector sits and how requests are routed.
[02:32] Samir: sure. high level: customer traffic hits MarketForge front-end, request sent to MarketForge connector which calls Redwood runtime. in Private mode the runtime lives in your VPC or on-prem cluster — so the connector communicates over an internal network with mTLS and token based auth; audit logs go to your SIEM and we push minimal metadata to the Redwood control plane for billing and rollouts.
[02:56] Maya: that sounds right. how do you handle fallback if capacity isn't available? e.g., do you route to hosted?
[03:02] Jules: yes we support smart routing policies — you can configure fallback to hosted or a compatible quantized model. for enterprise SLAs we typically pin to Dedicated to guarantee throughput.
[03:16] Connor: there was mention earlier of prefix/KV cache to save cost — does that require special config on our end?
[03:23] Samir: prefix caching is managed by the runtime; the connector can pass cache keys, but no heavy lift required. for best results we recommend annotating common prompts so the runtime can cache.
[03:35] [crosstalk] Priya: ok makes sense, mm-hmm.
[03:40] Jules: on the marketplace listing UX — do you have a preferred pricing unit? per-token, seat, or subscription?
[03:48] Maya: MarketForge typically likes subscription tiers but customers often ask for per-usage transparency. we'd like to offer both: a base subscription plus metered overage.
[03:58] Samir: we can support that. on our side we'll provide a price sheet mapping tokens to expected cost under typical workloads; we can include Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization in the listing.
[04:15] Connor: technical compliance: our legal team needs to see the data flow diagram and retention commitments. is there a standard SLA and data retention policy you can attach?
[04:23] Jules: yes we'll attach a draft SLA and the retention policy. retention can be set to 0 for private deployments — we can disable logs, or keep minimal auditing per your reqs.
[04:35] Priya: about SSO — do you support SCIM for user provisioning?
[04:38] Jules: yes, SCIM + SAML SSO supported for both hosted and private control plane. we'll include an SSO integration guide.
[04:47] Maya: do you have any partner co-marketing constraints? e.g., logos, press release cadence?
[04:51] Samir: typical: co-branded one-pager, joint blog post after pilot, and if you want marketplace featured placement we do a joint Go-to-Market plan. marketing can coordinate timing. we'll need your logo assets and a short 2-3 sentence blurb.
[05:06] Connor: network details — what's the preferred port and any firewall rules?
[05:10] Jules: connector uses HTTPS with mTLS over standard ports. for on-prem there are a few endpoints to allow to our control plane for billing and telemetry — we can put exact IP ranges in the ops checklist.
[05:25] Priya: do you provide a docker image or helm chart for the connector?
[05:28] Jules: both. we have a helm chart for k8s installs and a docker image for containerized deployments. we'll include the helm values example in the ref arch repo.
[05:38] Maya: are there any known limitations we should call out in the listing? latency guarantees with long context windows?
[05:43] Samir: yep, longer seq lengths can increase latency — we usually publish example latency for 512/1024 token workloads on the listing. also quantized models affect quality — we'll include model recommendations per use case.
[05:58] Connor: on the pilot — what does success look like? we proposed validating avg latency < 250ms for search workloads and end-to-end auth_flow working.
[06:07] Samir: that matches our suggested success criteria. for the pilot we'll run benchmarking with your sample prompts, log latency and cost and then produce a recommendations doc (batching, quantization) and a go/no-go.
[06:20] Priya: timeline — can we get a pilot started mid-November?
[06:24] Samir: yes if we get the listing draft and your infra details this week we'll aim to kick off the pilot by 2025-11-18.
[06:32] [10:05] Jules: (screen share) i'm pulling up the listing template now — screenshot placeholders, spec section, security checklist. link: https://redwood.example.com/partner/marketplace-template.pdf
[10:49] Maya: thanks, that's helpful. i'll flag this to our product marketing team.
[11:02] Connor: one more technical q — how are model upgrades handled in private? we don't want silent breaking changes.
[11:09] Jules: we do version pinning and rollouts; you can opt into auto-upgrades or keep a pinned model version. we also offer canary rollout capabilities and quality regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
[11:23] Priya: perfect. for the reference arch, can you include the diagram showing KMS, SIEM, and optional hosted fallback?
[11:30] Samir: yes, that's standard. Jules will draft the ref arch and we'll share as a draw.io and PDF.
[11:38] [20:01] Maya: ok let's recap next steps and owners.
[20:05] Samir: recap: Samir will send marketplace listing template + example screenshots; Jules will produce reference arch diagram and helm values; Connor will send network and KMS constraints; Priya will validate SSO/SCIM flows; MarketForge marketing to prepare co-branded one-pager. meet again next week for infra deep-dive.
[20:27] Maya: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[20:30] Samir: thanks — we'll follow up in email with links and the draft timelines.
[20:36] Connor: thanks all.
[20:40] [END]
